findings.summary: The Node build-stage recipe never copies the application source, so `npm run build` (and the runtime stage's `COPY --from=build /app/dist`) cannot succeed.
findings.evidence: "FROM node:20-alpine AS build","WORKDIR /app","COPY package*.json ./","RUN npm ci && npm run build" — and later "COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist"
findings.fix: Insert `COPY . .` between `RUN npm ci` and the build step, e.g. `COPY package*.json ./` / `RUN npm ci` / `COPY . .` / `RUN npm run build` — which also preserves the manifest-split caching the deck teaches.

findings.summary: Two Dockerfile-instruction sections are stranded at the end of page 1, leaving page 2 to jump from section 2 to section 5.
findings.evidence: Page 1 ends with "3. No Shell State Survives" (`RUN cd /app # dies with the container`) and "4. Chain What Depends" (`RUN apt-get update && \ apt-get install -y curl`), both Chapter-2 material placed after page 1's concluding callout. Page 2's headings then run "1. One Instruction, One Layer", "2. Ordering Is Semantic", "5. COPY vs ADD", "6. Context Ships First" — 3 and 4 are missing.
findings.fix: Move both sections onto page 2 between "2. Ordering Is Semantic" and "5. COPY vs ADD", restoring the 1–6 sequence.

findings.summary: The claim that the whole context directory is always tarred and uploaded describes the legacy builder, not BuildKit, which has been the default builder since Docker 23 and transfers only the files COPY/ADD actually reference.
findings.evidence: "Whole dir tarred and sent to the daemon pre-build", "3GB context = 3GB upload even for one COPY"
findings.fix: Rewrite as: the classic builder tars and ships the entire context up front; BuildKit (default since Docker 23) streams only the files matched by COPY/ADD, incrementally and cached between builds — so a 3GB directory costs 3GB only if an instruction copies it. Keep `.dockerignore` justified by cache busting and secret leakage, not just upload size.

findings.summary: The statement that the 127-layer limit is gone is false — overlay2 is still bounded by OverlayFS's 128 lowerdir limit and builds fail with "max depth exceeded".
findings.evidence: "Layer count is cheap — the 127-layer limit is gone"
findings.fix: Replace with: "Layer count is cheap up to a point — overlay2 still caps at 128 lower layers and the daemon rejects images past ~125 with 'max depth exceeded'."

findings.summary: The build-cache chapter opens at the bottom of page 2, so the page titled "The Build Cache" starts mid-chapter at section 3 with no key definition on it.
findings.evidence: Page 2 (titled "How the Dockerfile Builds Layers") ends with "1. How The Key Is Built" — "Cache key = parent layer digest + this instruction's own key" — and "2. Key Basis Per Instruction". Page 3, titled "The Build Cache: How It Decides to Reuse", opens with "3. Two Consequences", whose first bullet already assumes the key rule: "`RUN apt-get install -y curl` caches forever — stale software".
findings.fix: Move the "1. How The Key Is Built" paragraph and the "2. Key Basis Per Instruction" table to the top of page 3, ahead of "3. Two Consequences".

findings.summary: The allowlist `.dockerignore` example uses trailing inline comments, which the parser does not strip, so every annotated line becomes a literal pattern and the allowlist silently does nothing.
findings.evidence: ["*                  # deny everything","!src/","!package.json","!package-lock.json # new junk excluded"]
findings.fix: Move comments to their own lines (only a `#` in column 1 is a comment in `.dockerignore`): `# deny everything` / `*` / `!src/` / `!package.json` / `!package-lock.json`. As printed, `*` never matches and `package-lock.json` is never re-included.

findings.summary: The `--squash` sidebox misstates its behaviour: it squashes only the layers the build adds, keeps the base image's layers, and therefore does not destroy base-layer sharing.
findings.evidence: "Collapses every layer into one", "Loses cross-image base layer sharing"
findings.fix: State that `--squash` merges only newly built layers into one while the base image layers are retained and still shared, that it can double disk use (cache copy + squashed copy), and that it is an experimental legacy-builder flag ignored/unsupported under BuildKit — multi-stage is the supported alternative.

findings.summary: The claim that pip must compile C extensions from source on Alpine is outdated — musllinux wheels (PEP 656) are published for most major packages, including NumPy, pandas, matplotlib and cryptography.
findings.evidence: "manylinux wheels are glibc-only, so pip compiles C extensions from source." and "Python builds run 5-10x slower and pull in gcc"
findings.fix: Say manylinux wheels are glibc-only, but musllinux wheels (PEP 656) now cover most popular packages; the source-build penalty hits only projects that do not publish musllinux wheels — check your dependency set rather than assuming a 5–10x build.

findings.summary: "musl DNS: no `search` domains" is false — musl has supported `domain`/`search` in resolv.conf since 1.1.13 (2016), and the TCP-fallback gap was closed in musl 1.2.4 (Alpine 3.18+).
findings.evidence: "musl DNS: no `search` domains, TCP fallback edge cases"
findings.fix: Replace with the real remaining difference: musl supports `search`/`ndots`, but a name with at least `ndots` dots is tried only in the global namespace and never falls back to the search list (glibc does), and TCP fallback exists only on musl ≥ 1.2.4 / Alpine ≥ 3.18.

findings.summary: The suggested debug command does not open a shell: `sh` is passed as arguments to the image's ENTRYPOINT rather than replacing it.
findings.evidence: "example_code":["docker run --rm -it app:debug sh"] — answering "Why does `docker exec -it app sh` fail on my distroless image?"
findings.fix: Use `docker run --rm -it --entrypoint=sh app:debug` (or `--entrypoint=/busybox/sh`); the deck's own images set `ENTRYPOINT ["/app"]`, so the trailing `sh` would just be an argv to the app.

findings.summary: "ADD ... # ✗ no checksum" is outdated — ADD supports `--checksum=sha256:...` for remote URLs (Dockerfile syntax 1.6+, shipped with Docker 23).
findings.evidence: "ADD https://x/f.tgz /   # ✗ no checksum"
findings.fix: Show `ADD --checksum=sha256:$SHA https://x/f.tgz /` as the verified form (noting it applies to remote URLs only), and keep the curl+`sha256sum -c` recipe as the fallback for older syntax versions.

findings.summary: `COPY --chown` is described as saving a chmod layer; it sets ownership, and the separate `--chmod` flag sets permissions.
findings.evidence: "`COPY --chown=app:app` skips an extra chmod layer"
findings.fix: Change to "`COPY --chown=app:app` skips an extra `RUN chown -R` layer; use `COPY --chmod=` for modes" — and note that any later chown *or* chmod forces copy-up of every file it touches.

findings.fix: Replace the bullet with "Metadata instructions add no filesystem layer — they show as 0B rows in `docker history` because they only mutate the config JSON."

findings.summary: The same legacy-builder context claim is repeated as the framing for `.dockerignore`, which is inaccurate under the default BuildKit builder.
findings.evidence: "The CLI tars the context and ships it to the daemon before instruction one runs."
findings.fix: Reword to: the client exposes the context to the builder before instruction one runs — the classic builder tars all of it, BuildKit fetches only what COPY/ADD needs — and `.dockerignore` filters what is eligible either way.

findings.summary: The "Per-Tool No-Cache Flags" table lists entries that are not no-cache flags: `npm ci --omit=dev` only drops devDependencies and leaves npm's cache in the layer, and `go clean -modcache` is a command, not a flag.
findings.evidence: Table "Per-Tool No-Cache Flags" rows ["npm","ci --omit=dev"] and ["go","clean -modcache"]
findings.fix: Retitle the table "Per-Tool Slimming Flags" and fix the npm row to `npm ci --omit=dev && npm cache clean --force` (or a `--mount=type=cache` on /root/.npm), since `npm ci` alone still leaves ~/.npm in the image.
